models.name: VILA-U-7B
models.cls: Real model, quantized, codebook collapsed
models.verdict: Passes
models.sanity: Passes the sanity check. This is the model we use for the fixes.
models.note: Everything we claim about fixing hallucination rests on this model. It also has the lowest A2 mass of any model that passes, at 17.50, so it is the one that sets the ceiling on that threshold. Move A2 anywhere from 8 to 15 and nothing changes. Move it to 18 and VILA-U itself drops out.

models.name: Liquid-7B
models.cls: Real model, quantized, codebook collapsed
models.verdict: Passes, but stops answering when we switch L0 off
models.sanity: Fails the sanity check. We use it as evidence for the gates only.
models.note: Switching L0 off takes the yes-rate from 78% to 0%, and the model then writes nothing at all. The score looks better only because it stopped answering. We traced this inside the model: it loses the ability to respond to its input at all, rather than losing its grip on the image specifically.

models.name: Chameleon-7B
models.cls: Real model, quantized, codebook collapsed
models.verdict: Passes
models.sanity: Passes the sanity check. The second model we can actually fix.
models.note: This one leans towards saying no, answering yes only 22% of the time, and its codebook leans that way too. Oddly, L0 still pushes it towards yes. The no behaviour comes from L1 instead, and switching L1 off flips the yes-rate from 22.3% to 66.2%.

models.name: Anole-7B
models.cls: Real model, quantized, then trained to generate images
models.verdict: Passes, but stops answering when we switch L0 off
models.sanity: Fails the sanity check. We use it as evidence for the gates only.
models.note: This is Chameleon-7B after extra training to generate images, and it carries five times its parent's A2 mass. Training on quantized image tokens makes the problem stronger rather than leaving it alone.

models.name: Lumina-mGPT-7B
models.cls: Real model, quantized, held out when we set the thresholds
models.verdict: Passes, but its behaviour has no room to change
models.sanity: Not applicable. It already says yes only 0.07% of the time.
models.note: We never used this model to set the thresholds, so it is a real test of them. It has the strongest A2 signal of anything we measured, and switching L0 off changes nothing, because it already almost never says yes. Its weakest number is the carry half of A1, 0.623 at layer 20.

models.name: LLaVA-VQ K=1024
models.cls: We built it, quantized, sweeping codebook size
models.verdict: Passes, but its behaviour does not shift
models.note: The circuit appears but the model's behaviour does not shift. All four sizes end up using only about 80 to 160 codes, whatever we set.

models.name: LLaVA-VQ K=4096
models.cls: We built it, quantized, sweeping codebook size
models.verdict: Passes, and pushes the opposite way (unexplained)
models.note: The one we cannot explain. We checked its codebook entry by entry: it leans towards yes at 0.836, essentially the same as K=16384 at 0.864 and K=65536 at 0.870. Yet switching L0 off pushes it the opposite way from those two. The oddity is in what the fix does, not in the codebook.

models.name: LLaVA-VQ K=16384
models.cls: We built it, quantized, codebook collapsed
models.verdict: Passes
models.note: The model we built to test cause. We took LLaVA-1.6, froze the language model and the image encoder, and swapped only the part that converts the image for one that quantizes. 2000 steps on 50k captions. Its yes-rate climbs to 85.5%, and switching L0 off drops it to 14.1%.

models.name: LLaVA-VQ K=65536
models.cls: We built it, quantized, sweeping codebook size
models.verdict: Passes, pushes towards yes, weakly
models.note: The second model we tested on full captions. It makes up objects at 52.5%, five times VILA-U's rate, on the same backbone. Switching L0 off cuts that to 42.7%. Per image that drop is not statistically solid, so this model supports the captioning result rather than carrying it.

models.name: LLaVA-VQ-FSQ v1
models.cls: We built it, with a quantizer that cannot collapse
models.verdict: Passes, and pushes the opposite way
models.note: This quantizer cannot collapse, by design, and the circuit still appears, pushing the model the other way. That is our evidence that collapse is not required. A3 does not apply here: the quantizer uses a fixed grid, so there is no learned codebook to snap between. Its A1 start value of 0.450 sets the ceiling on that threshold. At 0.45 it would drop out.

models.name: LLaVA-VQ-FSQ v2
models.cls: We built it, with a quantizer that cannot collapse
models.verdict: Rejected: nothing happens early
models.note: It shifts the model the same way v1 does, yes-rate up 53.3 points and AMBER down 19.8, but we cannot find an early event in it: 0.379, and the drift first passes 0.4 only at layer 14. So the two versions agree on what the model does and disagree on why. That is why we do not credit the direction flip to the early circuit on its own.

models.name: LLaVA-MLP (matched-compute control)
models.cls: We built it, without quantizing
models.verdict: Rejected: nothing happens early, and no behaviour change
models.note: This is the control that makes the whole chain necessary. Same data, same steps, same settings, same frozen language model as the quantizing version. Only the converter differs. It passes A2 with mass 25.52, because a healthy Vicuna-7B already sends early attention to the image. But it fails both halves of A1, and switching L0 off does nothing. The route was already there. Quantizing adds the signal that travels down it.

models.name: UniTok
models.cls: Real model, quantized through a token embedder
models.verdict: Rejected: nothing happens early
models.note: It clears the A2 threshold at 18.23 but nothing happens early: the drift only reaches 0.4 at layer 13. Along with FSQ v2, this is one of the two models that stop us lowering the A1 threshold.

models.name: Show-o-1.3B
models.cls: Real model, image codes added to the text vocabulary
models.verdict: Rejected: nothing happens early
models.note: The drift never gets close to the threshold anywhere in the model. There is no single event to switch off, so we probe it across a range of layers instead of one.

models.name: SEED-LLaMA-8B
models.cls: Real model, image codes added to the text vocabulary
models.verdict: Rejected: nothing happens early
models.note: Same story as Show-o. Nothing reaches the threshold early on, so we probe it across a range of layers instead of one.

models.name: Emu3-Chat
models.cls: Real model, quantized, no separate converter
models.verdict: Rejected: the early event does not carry
models.note: The only model where the early spike fails to carry. It passes A2 easily at 48.44 and has a real early event at 0.435, but by the second half of the network the drift is down to 0.215. This is the case the second half of A1 exists for.

models.name: Qwen-VQ (induced control)
models.cls: We built it, quantized, codebook collapsed
models.verdict: Rejected: too little early attention on the image
models.note: The mirror image of the MLP control. Its codebook collapses badly and it passes both A1 and A3, and the circuit still never formed. It just answers no to everything. Together with FSQ v1 this shows a collapsed codebook is neither needed nor enough.

models.name: Janus-Pro-7B
models.cls: Reads images as continuous features, not codes
models.verdict: Rejected: no codebook to test
models.note: For understanding images it uses continuous features, not codes, so there is no codebook to snap between and it fails A3 outright. Its low A2 mass of 13.57 is beside the point. It does pass A1, and that is the lesson: any model that looks hard at the image carries image damage forward, whether or not it quantizes. A1 on its own cannot tell the two kinds apart.

models.name: VILA-U-MLP (reverse-ablation control)
models.cls: Continuous adapter on a model pretrained with quantizing
models.verdict: Rejected: no codebook to test
models.note: Putting the problem in takes 2000 steps. Taking it out does not work in the same 2000 steps. We trained a normal continuous adapter on top of VILA-U, which was already pretrained with quantization. A1 still passes, L0 mass went up rather than down, from 17.50 to 20.53, and the yes-rate went from 81% to 99.2%. We mark it a fail on A3 because a continuous adapter leaves no codebook to test, but the gates it does pass are the point.

models.name: LLaVA-1.6
models.cls: Reads images as continuous features (control)
models.verdict: Rejected: reads images as continuous features
models.note: The healthy model everything we built starts from. Switching L0 off does nothing to it at all.

models.name: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct
models.cls: Reads images as continuous features (control)
models.verdict: Rejected: reads images as continuous features
models.note: The same change that helps VILA-U wrecks this model. Getting opposite results on two different architectures is hard to explain unless the mechanism is real.
